questions.stem: You are containerizing Tidewater Ask for AgentCore Runtime with the HTTP protocol. Which two are part of the container contract? Choose two.
options: Serve on 0.0.0.0 port 8080 (default) with POST /invocations and GET /ping
Build an ARM64 container image
Expose port 443 with TLS terminated in the container
Implement /healthz returning plain text OK
Run as a Lambda handler function
questions.explanation: The HTTP protocol contract is port 8080 by default, /invocations and /ping, on an ARM64 container. TLS terminates at the service; /healthz and Lambda handlers are not part of it.

questions.stem: Your /ping returns {"status": "Healthy", "time_of_last_update": now()} on every call. What goes wrong?
options: Nothing, it is the documented format
The idle session timeout never fires, so sessions live until max lifetime and can exhaust your session quota
The runtime treats the agent as unhealthy
Invocations are rejected with 409
questions.explanation: time_of_last_update must change only when the status changes. A timestamp that advances on every ping looks like a continuous status change and keeps sessions alive.

questions.stem: An invocation kicks off a background reindex that runs after the response is sent. What should /ping report meanwhile?
options: Healthy
HealthyBusy, which keeps the session active while the work runs
Unhealthy
Nothing; return 204
questions.explanation: HealthyBusy says the agent is operational but busy with async work, and the session is kept alive. Healthy would let the idle timeout stop the microVM mid-task.

questions.stem: The agent code needs the caller's tenant_id claim. The runtime uses a customJWTAuthorizer. How does the token reach the container?
options: It is always forwarded in X-Amzn-Bedrock-AgentCore-Runtime-Session-Id
Add Authorization to the runtime's request header allowlist; it can be forwarded when the runtime has a custom JWT authorizer
Call Cognito from the container with the user's password
Read it from the payload the web app sends
questions.explanation: Authorization is forwarded only if allowlisted, and only for runtimes configured with a custom JWT authorizer, which validated it first. The payload is attacker-controlled and the session header carries the session id.

learn.label: Pass custom headers to AgentCore Runtime

questions.stem: A session on AgentCore Runtime (microVM) sits idle for 20 minutes with default settings, then the user asks again with the same session id. What happens?
options: The request fails with ResourceNotFoundException
The session had stopped after the 15-minute default idle timeout; the next invocation provisions a new microVM for the same session id, and in-memory state is gone
The old microVM resumes with its memory intact
Sessions never stop before 8 hours
questions.explanation: Defaults are 15 minutes idle and 8 hours max lifetime. A stopped session becomes active again on the next invocation on new compute, so durable state belongs in AgentCore Memory (or session storage), not in process memory.

questions.stem: A Gateway Lambda target named tw_orders exposes lookup_order. What does the function see in context.client_context.custom["bedrockAgentCoreToolName"]?
options: lookup_order
tw_orders___lookup_order (target name, three underscores, tool name)
tw_orders/lookup_order
arn:aws:bedrock-agentcore:...:tool/lookup_order
questions.explanation: The Gateway prefixes the tool with the target name and a triple-underscore delimiter; the docs' boilerplate strips it with index('___'). Splitting on single underscores breaks tools whose names contain underscores.

questions.stem: What is the Lambda event when the Gateway invokes a Lambda target for tools/call?
options: The full MCP JSON-RPC request
A map of the tool's inputSchema properties to their values (the tool arguments)
An API Gateway proxy event
The user's JWT claims
questions.explanation: The event is just the arguments; metadata (tool name, gateway id, target id, MCP message id) is in the context's client_context.custom.

questions.stem: You scope the runtime role with bedrock-agentcore:namespace conditions. Which value matches what AgentCore Memory acts on?
options: tenant/acme-foods/actor/alice
/tenant/acme-foods/actor/alice
/tenant/acme-foods/actor/alice/ (one leading and one trailing slash)
Any of these; Memory normalizes IAM values
questions.explanation: Memory stores namespaces normalized with a leading and a trailing slash, and IAM condition values must use the same form; omitting a slash means the policy does not match. The trailing slash also prevents prefix collisions such as alice vs alice2.

questions.stem: A semantic strategy uses /org/{orgname}/actor/{actorId}/ with a custom namespace key orgname. Which two are true? Choose two.
options: Values are supplied per event in CreateEvent extractionConfig.namespaceVariables
Custom variable keys and values must be lowercase
If orgname is missing, CreateEvent fails
Custom variables replace actorId
Values are read from the caller's JWT automatically
questions.explanation: Custom variables are declared as namespaceKeys on the memory and supplied in extractionConfig.namespaceVariables; keys and values are lowercase. If a referenced variable is missing, the event is still stored but long-term extraction is skipped for that strategy (NamespaceResolutionFailure metric).

questions.stem: Which two statements about AgentCore Memory are correct? Choose two.
options: CreateEvent stores conversation events per actor and session (short-term memory)
Memory strategies extract long-term records from events asynchronously, and RetrieveMemoryRecords searches them in a namespace
Long-term records are written synchronously before CreateEvent returns
Memory has no notion of actors; isolation must be done in the prompt
RetrieveMemoryRecords requires the session id
questions.explanation: Events are short-term, scoped by actorId and sessionId; strategies (semantic, summary, user preference, custom) extract long-term records into namespaces in the background, which you search with RetrieveMemoryRecords.

questions.stem: A customer wants a stateless classifier: one Converse call per support email, no tools, no session. Runtime or Lambda?
options: AgentCore Runtime, because all agents must run there
A plain Lambda calling Converse is enough; Runtime pays off for multi-step, long-running, session-isolated agents
Neither; use InvokeModel from the browser
Runtime, because Lambda cannot call Bedrock
questions.explanation: Runtime gives per-session microVM isolation, long sessions and agent-framework hosting. A single stateless call does not need it, and an FDE should say so.

questions.stem: You write the Tidewater Ask infrastructure in CDK for a client. Which statement about AgentCore constructs is current?
options: Everything is in @aws-cdk/aws-bedrock-agentcore-alpha
The L2 constructs are stable in aws-cdk-lib/aws-bedrockagentcore; only Policy is still in the alpha package
There is no CDK support; use raw CloudFormation
Use the deprecated starter toolkit instead
questions.explanation: The AgentCore L2 constructs moved to aws-cdk-lib/aws-bedrockagentcore; Policy (PolicyEngine, Policy) remains alpha. Check that before suggesting an alpha dependency in a client repo.

questions.stem: Traces from the AgentCore runtime do not show up in CloudWatch. What one-time setup is commonly missing?
options: Enabling X-Ray Insights
Turning on CloudWatch Transaction Search (and, for memory spans, enabling tracing on the memory)
Creating a Firehose stream
Adding a CloudWatch dashboard
questions.explanation: AgentCore observability needs CloudWatch Transaction Search enabled once per account to view spans and traces; memory spans also need tracing enabled at memory creation.

questions.stem: Security wants a deterministic rule: the agent may call create_refund only for amounts under 500 USD, regardless of what the model decides. Which AgentCore capability fits?
options: Memory strategies
AgentCore Policy (Cedar rules evaluated on tool calls at the Gateway)
Evaluations
Observability
questions.explanation: Policy evaluates Cedar rules on tool calls outside the model, so the rule holds even if the model is steered. Evaluations score quality; they do not block calls.
